remainingEvidence: Nothing built today discriminates convergence from the idempotence C13-BLUEPRINT-REMATERIALIZE already verifies. Its selector proves re-applying one unchanged Blueprint reconciles to a semantic no-op, which is f(f(x)) = f(x) for one input; path-independence needs a differential harness that applies one Blueprint to a Scope by at least two admissible issue orders and from at least two different prior managed states, then asserts one identical Blueprint-managed record set once the pending set is empty. An implementation that reached the declared state only from an empty Scope must fail it

The pending set has to be carried by the reconciliation outcome rather than computed alongside it, so that converged is that set being empty rather than a separate report a host can get wrong. Verification requires the outcome type to hold the obligations and a mutation that states convergence while an obligation stands to break a cited test; a boolean flag set next to a nonempty obligation list satisfies the prose and must not satisfy the atom

Each of the four stated deferrals needs its own obligation-shape evidence — record, reason, and discharging condition all named: a reliance hold under C13-FACET-DEPENDENCY-ORDER, each draining Invocation item under C13-FACET-WITHDRAWAL-DRAIN, each unadmitted RouteReservation terminalized by a rejected RouteDelivery, and a Package retained under SPEC 5.2. No current test exercises any of them, and the Package case additionally has no coverage of the Session, tree-checkpoint, and Snapshot pin holders

The rejected-reconciliation clause is what stops converging from becoming an excuse, so it needs the strongest negative evidence: a divergence expressible as no pending obligation — a withdrawal set the host cannot compute, or a retired Slot declaration still holding an entry attributed to a retained Facet — must be refused at validation before package code loads, on the no-code-loaded terms C13-BLUEPRINT-VALIDATE-BEFORE-LOAD already tests, and must never be admitted and left pending

The managed-set scoping needs its own test because it is what makes the endpoint a function at all: an adopted manual edit must appear as a change to the Blueprint, and a host that marks an adopted record Blueprint-managed without a declaring Blueprint must be rejected. src/definition/materializer.ts#LocalMaterializer marks managed state but has no adoption path to discriminate

Recorded honestly rather than deferred: this rule's paragraph tightened the SPEC 9.3 retention condition from 'no Run references it' to the full SPEC 5.2 pin-holder set, so C13-BLUEPRINT-RUN-PINS now carries anchored text whose Session, Turn, tree-checkpoint, and Snapshot cases its two verified selectors do not exercise. W4 owes that atom a pin-holder test, and this atom cannot be verified while the condition it names is under-covered by its neighbour

remainingEvidence: The Binding foundation is present: the Tenant-owned Binding record carries canonical, unique (SecretRef, endpoint) custody facts, validates each SecretRef source against its exact TenantId, preserves or explicitly rotates those facts through the Binding mutation path, and restores the same record through Memory and SQLite storage. This is constituent data in the Binding codec, not a second durable custody record or mirror

The remaining authority work is to bind that complete Binding snapshot to the target-owned request and Tenant-issued permit used for cross-Actor mediated admission. Tenant issuance must compare it with the current canonical Binding in the Tenant transaction, and target consumption must authenticate the exact retained request and permit without a synchronous cross-Actor read or a copied Binding authority plane

The remaining provider work is a concrete credential-isolation adapter that accepts only authenticated permit/request evidence, rejects inactive, substituted, guest, cross-Tenant, SecretRef, consumer, and endpoint mismatches, and injects raw credential material directly into transport. Confirmed custody refusal must become a failed attempted Receipt, while unavailable or unknown provider outcomes remain indeterminate. Redirect/repoint behavior, restart/replay, raw-secret non-escape, and the deployed Cloudflare boundary still need behavioral evidence before this atom can be verified

remainingEvidence: The relation does not exist as data anywhere: no Package record, manifest, or codec carries a dependency set, so the first obligation is the declared `{ id: PackageId, range: CompatRange }` set on the Package shape, its codec with decode rejection of a duplicate id, and a restore round-trip through the stores the Package shape already uses

The closure claim is the load-bearing one and is currently unfalsifiable. C13-RUN-PINS-PACKAGES rejects an incomplete or duplicated closure but compares it against nothing, so verification needs a check that RunPins.packages equals the transitive closure of the declared relation from the Blueprint's packages list resolved to exact versions, and a mutation supplying a complete-looking closure that is not that closure must be rejected rather than accepted

Pre-load rejection needs two negative tests on the no-code-loaded terms C13-BLUEPRINT-VALIDATE-BEFORE-LOAD already establishes: an unsatisfiable range, and a dependency on a Package the Blueprint does not install, each rejecting the Blueprint with no package code resolved or evaluated

The non-derivation clause is checkable today and must be tested rather than assumed: a dependency names a PackageId and a BindingRequirement names a FacetPackageId (src/facets/manifest.ts#BindingRequirement), which C13-RUN-PIN-IDENTITY-TYPES already forbids converting or comparing by string value. Evidence must show a binding requirement never becomes a dependency and a dependency never satisfies a binding requirement

Termination under a cyclic declared relation needs a mutual-dependency pair proving the closure computation is finite and unique by PackagePin.id, because this rule deliberately does not reject a package-level cycle — only the reliance cycle of C13-FACET-DEPENDENCY-ORDER is rejected, and an implementation that conflated the two relations would wrongly refuse a legitimate Blueprint

The declaration half is built and discrimination-tested. PlacementPolicy carries `backings` (src/definition/placement.ts#AuthoredCodeBackingPolicy), a partial map from the closed §4.7 consumer set to an opaque AuthoredCodeBackingId, read through PlacementPolicy.backingFor(consumer, profileDefault); an unmapped consumer takes the substrate profile's declared default and never another offered backing. test/definition/authored-code-backing.test.ts covers it under this atom's id, and four mutations — ignoring the declaration, sending an unmapped consumer to a declared backing, dropping the mapping on encode, and opening the consumer set — each break a cited test.

Worker Loader is the only §4.7 backing currently implemented by the Cloudflare package. It loads the isolate with `globalOutbound: null`, `disallow_importable_env`, and an `env` holding one entrypoint stub per delegated Binding and nothing else, all three exercised against real workerd in the cloudflare lane.

The former dispatch-namespace adapter was removed because it could not establish the abstract AuthoredCodeBacking contract it claimed: outbound posture is a property of the binding's deployed outbound Worker, not of `DispatchNamespace.get()`. Restoring the §10.2 dispatch backing requires a configured deny-all outbound Worker, the exact deployed binding, and a real substrate test proving both `fetch` and `connect` are unavailable while passed Binding capabilities remain callable.

C13-PLACEMENT-DYNAMIC-NO-EGRESS remains an explicit prerequisite. Verification also requires ownership-correct integration evidence connecting the W4 declaration to every W8 backing the profile actually offers; Worker Loader evidence cannot stand in for an unimplemented dispatch backing.

The rule is enforced by domain construction at the substrate (SPEC §1.5: policy code inside the domain is not a security boundary); W4's definition plane can declare only the dynamic mode and cannot establish the network posture of a W8 backing

No substrate-neutral interface, nominal token, or local reference can prove zero ambient egress. Verification requires ownership-correct integration between the W4 placement decision and every concrete backing the selected profile offers, together with evidence from each backing's real enforcement boundary

For Worker Loader, adversarial code running in the real substrate must fail both global fetch and connect while an explicitly passed Binding remains callable. A dispatch-namespace backing additionally requires the exact deployed namespace and deny-all outbound Worker configuration; local fakes do not satisfy either obligation
